video_title: How Steph Curry Can Decide The Warriors' Future + Major Questions For Pistons & FIBA Qualifiers

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Steph Curry's contract extension options with the Golden State Warriors
quotes.excerpt: Steph Curry became eligible to sign a contract extension. Steph hasn't really had any super interesting contract moments.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Over the weekend, Steph Curry became eligible to sign a contract extension. Steph hasn't really had any super interesting contract moments in his career, other than probably when he signed his first extension. That enabled Kevin Durant to come, probably enabled Shawn Livingston to come, enabled Andre Iguodala to come.

text_blocks.speaker: Anthony Slater
text_blocks.text: Four for 44. It set up a dynasty, really.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: That enabled Clay Thompson to come. All of those little pieces and parts made it possible for Durant later on.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors' cap space flexibility and potential future moves
quotes.excerpt: They are not negotiating with Steph Curry right now. They are saying, here's your menu, pick off your menu.

text_blocks.speaker: Anthony Slater
text_blocks.text: The Warriors have presented him these options. The one thing I will tell you from talking to people this weekend is they are not negotiating with Steph Curry right now. They are saying, you can do this, you can do this, you can do this. If you want the one-year max, if you want the two-year max, if you want to wait, here's your menu, pick off your menu.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: If he took his max now, Bobby Marks has told me it takes him to about 45 million in cap space, which is still a ton of cap space. It just limits all of what they can do. But at the same time, two other notes on their cap space next summer: the Kevon Looney extension changes that, which will probably be more of a conversation for September, October, but it matters. And then Kristaps Porzingis is owed 20 million next year, but only 3 million guaranteed. So while you say 45, you could add 17 million to that if you cut Kristaps Porzingis.

text_blocks.speaker: Anthony Slater
text_blocks.text: How much cap space do you think they need to bring Jonathan Kuminga back?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: That's a negotiation with Joe Lacob.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The need for a Jonathan Kuminga contract countdown clock
quotes.excerpt: I want a graphic right here that has number of days until Jonathan Kuminga's next free agency.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Please talk to our producers about, I want a graphic right here that has number of days until Jonathan Kuminga's next free agency. I want it as we go, I don't care if it's November, January, I want a clock. Actually, an actual hour clock, days, months, days, hours, clicking it down. It's going to be great, can't wait.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I just want to get in an early Kuminga reference just to get Wendy's blood boiling.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren and the Pistons' contract negotiation standoff
quotes.excerpt: It's basically just a staring contest that's continuing into September.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: McMahon, I believe you have a story that's posting when this podcast comes out on Tuesday on Jalen Duren?

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Yeah, and it's basically just a staring contest that's continuing into September, which is not unprecedented or even out of the realm of the norm for a restricted free agent. Josh Giddey didn't sign last year until I think like September 9th or something like that. But this is an unprecedented situation for a restricted free agent who was an All-Star, was a third team All-NBA player, for a guy who was a major driving force in a 60-win team.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The worst-case scenario for the Pistons regarding Jalen Duren
quotes.excerpt: You're going to leave 170, 180 million guaranteed dollars on the table. Obviously that is a worst case scenario.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: So you're going to leave 170, 180 million guaranteed dollars on the table. Obviously that is a worst case scenario for the Pistons, because then you're not even really getting Jalen Duren this season. You're getting this version of him that is constantly thinking about his next contract.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Yeah, this is a classic case with back of the envelope math that restricted free agents down the years have all done. Like, boy, to be an unrestricted free agent with a whole bunch of cap space out there, I would have, I mean, he would, if he was healthy, Jalen Duren as an unrestricted free agent would have a deal within minutes.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of toxic offer sheets on team negotiations
quotes.excerpt: You can't overpay a player, especially at a high dollar figure, it knee-caps you.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: I've been around teams like where this has been the case. If you get to training camp and Duren is like forced into a situation and a Sar Thompson is annoyed, like, you got like, I understand especially in the apron era that you got to, you can't overpay a player, especially at a high dollar figure, it knee-caps you. And I'm not saying that you should just do it to make your players all nice and happy. Teams that have done that have gotten into trouble. I'm just saying, I've been in training camps multiple times where there were multiple players upset about their contracts and it absolutely poisons the whole well.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Yeah, and so you know, you've got that situation. Obviously, Kade is on his supermax deal. It's almost like him being All-NBA the final year of his rookie contract, they're being punished for that. This is by the way, I still, the next CBA, I don't think supermax stuff should count towards apron and tax. I don't think that's fair, but that's a tangent.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The rarity of All-Star players in the current draft class
quotes.excerpt: There's four guys in this draft class who have been All-Stars: Paolo Banchero, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, and Jalen Duren.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: So, the starting set, there's four guys in this draft class who have been All-Stars: Paolo Banchero, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, and Jalen Duren. Those three guys all agreed to extensions last summer, right? They all ended up at the 25% max, which is 41 and change, almost 42, right? So again, that, he's looking at, I can't even get the 25% that those guys are getting and I'm like, you're asking me to take, I don't know if the, what it was, six, seven, whatever million below that.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: I understand, but he had, he had offers that he turned down. So that's the, that's the little bit of leverage that Jalen Duren and his reps have right now.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of non-tax years for team roster flexibility
quotes.excerpt: It needs to be a non-tax year because you want to push any potential repeater penalty.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: But it needs to be a non-tax year because you want to push any potential repeater penalty.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Yes. Yes. Well, here's the other thing about the Pistons. It, you know, actions over words, right? If you look at the contracts that the Pistons have signed, um, a lot of their contracts have flexibility built into them, non-guaranteed years for, so the the deal they gave John Collins this, uh, season, it was three years and 50 something, but only the first year is guaranteed.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The historical context of toxic offer sheets in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: Back when I was a kid, this was all the rage, toxic offer sheets.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Back when I was a kid, this was all the rage, toxic offer sheets. Over the years they went away. Now I've been around a while now, this is my 24th year covering the NBA and, you know, they used to like do these things where they used to put these poison pills and stuff. You remember the Jeremy Lin, the whole Jeremy Lin thing with the way they squeezed the Knicks, Daryl Morey, you know, doing a poison pill offer sheet. Um, this was just recently in the news a little bit this summer because Wesley Matthews, um, he was on a podcast and he was telling the story of his contract when he was with the Jazz and the Blazers signed him to this like 5-year, 35 million dollar deal, which you know.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: He was an undrafted free agent who stuck with the Jazz, was productive and then went into, uh, restricted free agency right after his rookie year.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of qualifying offers on player contract leverage
quotes.excerpt: If you're Jalen Duren and his reps, that's a little bit of of your leverage.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I do want to hit on one, you mentioned the Kings, and that's obviously like if you're Jalen Duren and his reps, that's a little bit of of your leverage. The threat of the qualifying offer and there's going to be a max market for us.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: It was noted to me, again, this is from a, an exec in the West, so I want to make it clear this wasn't people in Detroit saying it, but it's one thing to put a max offer sheet on the table when you're getting off a contract that you're trying to get off of. You know, it's one thing to shed Sabonis's contract and put a max number on the table or, you know, shed LaVine's or, you know, what it cost them a pick all, you know, at least, right? But it's another thing just to straight up commit a max deal with no money going out the door.
